solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Comrades of branch members accepting different function

indicators.note: the branch-and-members pair takes in the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: br. is the standard abbreviation for branch
arms are limbs, members of the body
other means different
sin is short for sine, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Fellow members of a local branch who disagree over what their job is.
explanation.walkthrough: Br. is a dictionary abbreviation for branch; sine is the trig function, shortened to sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothers in arms are soldiers fighting side by side, hence close comrades.

clue.text: Judges involved in substantial trial

indicators.note: the judges piece is set inside the substantial one

parts.note: real means substantial, having substance
a judge hears a case, so hears

explanation.surface: Judges take part in a major court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' suggests a court; it is a practice run.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a trial performance, a practice run before the real thing.

clue.text: Part of joint group that plays up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: A member of a band that plays up in the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a bar; it is a woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue of a mortise-and-tenon woodwork join.

clue.text: Leaves country as armies get mobilised

indicators.note: mobilised troops are moved and reorganised, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People flee abroad as troops are called up.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to depart one's homeland to settle abroad.

clue.text: Rent place on the coast

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., a port city on Croatia's Adriatic coast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as payment for housing, especially beside 'place'; here it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear in fabric, and Split is a Croatian seaside city.

clue.text: Close to large settlement, including good retirement cover

parts.note: nigh means near, close

indicators.note: the settlement takes in the good letter

parts.note: a town is a large settlement

explanation.surface: A retirement home near a big town with good amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests old age; it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is worn in bed, a garment covering someone who has retired for the night.

clue.text: Royal Academy books international legal expert

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy of Arts
b is book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: The Royal Academy hires a lawyer with an international practice.
explanation.walkthrough: A rabbi is a scholar of Jewish law, which is why 'legal expert' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is trained in Jewish religious law and teaches its interpretation.

clue.text: Manual work that's not recognised for what it is?

definitions.text: Manual work that's not recognised for what it is?

parts.words: Manual work that's not recognised for what it is?
parts.note: manual work is literally done by hand, and a conjuror's trick is meant to go unnoticed

explanation.definitionFit: A magician's deft hand trickery deceives the audience, so it is handiwork not seen for what it is.

clue.text: Vicar with epilepsy condemned to make meaningless gesture

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vicar suffering epilepsy is condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay lip service is to voice support without acting on it, an empty gesture.

clue.text: Artist's first and second layer of greyish colour

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Artist's is taken

parts.note: its first letter
a hen is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: A painter applies a first and a second coat of a grey shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' looks like a coat of paint, but it is a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a pale grey colour, like ash, so it means of greyish colour.

clue.text: Unreadable introduction of authoritative work becomes bad for one

indicators.note: the opening letter of the authoritative work is the one being changed
the opening letter turns into something else, a replacement

parts.note: the Bible is the archetypal authoritative book
ill means bad
e.g. (for example) is 'for one'

explanation.surface: An introduction to a weighty text is so badly written it cannot be read.
explanation.walkthrough: The B that opens BIBLE is replaced by ILL + EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegible handwriting or print cannot be deciphered, so it is unreadable.

clue.text: One inclined to absorb reading, writing or arithmetic

definitions.text: One inclined to absorb reading, writing or arithmetic

indicators.note: the inclined one takes the letter in, so it goes inside

parts.note: a leaner is one who leans, or is inclined
each is one of the three Rs of basic schooling, so R

explanation.surface: A pupil keen to pick up the basics of school.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic) are the basics of primary education; one R goes inside LEANER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil absorbing the three Rs is a student, someone still being taught.

clue.text: Expressing disapproval is no good after everyone plays

indicators.note: the no-good letters come after the everyone-plays piece

parts.note: tutti is the musical direction for all performers to play

explanation.surface: Clicking the tongue at a band where everyone plays at once.
explanation.walkthrough: TUTTI is the score marking telling the whole orchestra to play.
explanation.definitionFit: To tut is to make a clicking sound of disapproval, so tutting is expressing it.

clue.text: Remix tapes for Pulp

indicators.note: to remix a recording is to rework it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reworking tapes by the Britpop band Pulp.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulp looks like the band in a music surface; it is the definition, a soft mash.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste and pulp are both soft, moist mashed substances, near synonyms.

clue.text: Unconventional description of the letter D?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: a capital D is a half-circle whose centre lies on its straight edge, not in the middle of the shape

explanation.walkthrough: In engineering an eccentric is off-centre; the D's curve is centred on its straight back, so the letter is literally off-centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means odd or unusual, and literally means not having its centre in the middle.

clue.text: Radical, potentially harmful flaw is concealed by test's limitations

indicators.note: the flaw and is are hidden between the outer letters of the test
limits are edges, so only the outer letters of test are used

parts.note: the word test, whose edges are taken
an error is a flaw

explanation.surface: A dangerous defect lurks within the boundaries of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on test's is just possessive; only the first and last letters of test itself are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrorist is an extremist who threatens violence, a radical who may do harm.

clue.text: Engineers face new church hall?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a side is a face of something
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Engineers confront the prospect of a new church hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A hall can be a grand house, so it is an example of a home; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall is a large country house or a student building, a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Counting on dining club almost going bust

indicators.note: going bust means breaking up, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the last letter of club is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Relying on a dinner club that's close to bankruptcy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counting on' reads as one phrase meaning relying on; only 'Counting' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Including means counting something as part of the total.

clue.text: Mistakes caught in only one text message

indicators.note: caught goes inside the only-one pair

parts.note: sole means only
I is the Roman numeral one
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an SMS is a text message

explanation.surface: Errors spotted in a single text.
explanation.walkthrough: SMS (Short Message Service) is the technical name for a mobile phone text.
explanation.definitionFit: Solecisms are grammatical blunders or breaches of etiquette, so they are mistakes.

clue.text: See 9
I'm surprised about new revolutionary chip

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
ca. (circa) means about

explanation.surface: Someone startled by a radical new microchip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chip' suggests computing; it is a tortilla chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually topped with cheese, an example of a chip.

clue.text: See 8
Distilled wine contains brandy

indicators.note: the wine holds the brandy within it

parts.note: red is wine
fine is a French brandy (fine champagne)

explanation.surface: A distilled wine has brandy in it, like a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine is a name for a French brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled and refined both describe something purified, made purer by processing.

clue.text: Central point from clues regularly ignored

indicators.note: every other letter is skipped, leaving the alternate letters

explanation.surface: A crossword hint about the key point to be drawn from clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is the centre of interest or activity, the central point.

clue.text: Belief in God exists in hearts of eldest women

indicators.note: in places the heart of exists inside the hearts of the other two words
the heart of a word is its middle letter or letters, here taken from all three words

explanation.surface: Faith lives on in the hearts of the oldest women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts of' serves all three words, and 'in' sets the heart of exists between the other two hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is belief in a creator who does not intervene in the world.

clue.text: Pervert finally led Hecuba astray

indicators.note: the final letter of the word led
going astray means wandering out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer leads Hecuba, Queen of Troy, off the right path.
explanation.walkthrough: D (from led) then the anagram of Hecuba.
explanation.definitionFit: To debauch someone is to corrupt them morally, so it means to pervert.

clue.text: Elementary combination of disrespect and rudeness

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an alloy combining the elements copper and zinc

explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' hints at simplicity; it refers to chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is a copper-zinc alloy, and informally means brazen cheek or nerve.

clue.text: Offensive sound almost brought back having to suffer before

indicators.note: the suffer piece comes before the sound piece

parts.note: to incur is to suffer a cost or loss

indicators.note: brought back means reversed, so the shortened sound is read backwards
almost means the last letter of the sound word is cut

parts.note: a noise is a sound

explanation.surface: An offensive noise mostly returns, having to be endured first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective meaning rude; it is the noun, a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a military attack, and an incursion is a raid into hostile territory.

clue.text: Strange position adopted by article

indicators.note: the article takes in the position, so it goes inside

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the lie of something is its position

explanation.surface: An odd stance taken up by a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or unfamiliar, hence strange.

clue.text: Laissez-faire attitude to finance freedom of movement?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a relaxed view of money, which arrives and leaves without worry
second meaning, playful: things coming and going freely

explanation.walkthrough: Freedom of movement sounds like an EU policy; the question mark marks the playful reading of a phrase about coming and going.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes casual acceptance of gain and loss, especially of money that is spent as quickly as it arrives.
